Sam D: quick heads-up — ran into a puzzling entrypoint resolution mismatch between Node and the edge sample app when using the dual-package layout. Node consumers get the CJS build, edge runtime resolves to ESM but then our typings vanish and import shape is wrong. anyone seen this? :thinking_face:

Ben K: can you paste your package.json exports snippet? might be a conditional-exports precedence thing.

Sam D: sure — minimal repro from the sample app: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
Edge runtime (vercel edge) resolves `import` and works at runtime, but TS in consumer projects can't find types and `default` vs named import shape differs. Node (12/16) consumers are fine.

Chandra R: two quick suspects: 1) types entrypoint not declared under exports, 2) TS compiler/moduleResolution picks up different resolution on edge (esmodule interop). Do you have `types` field in package.json or `./dist/esm/index.d.ts` exported?

Sam D: we only have top-level "types": "dist/index.d.ts" in package.json. the .d.ts exists but when the sample runs on edge, runtime works but consumers (TS) doing `import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'` see no default and no types.

Frank P: almost certainly conditional exports; some bundlers/edge resolvers evaluate conditions differently. Try adding explicit types export: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  }
}
```
That can force typings for environments that read exports. also check `typesVersions` for TS path fallback.

Sam D: good idea — will try. fyi repro repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/entrypoint-interop (link to branch with failing sample). CI also flagged bundle smoke.

DevBot: sample-ci/sample-entrypoint-interop — build failed on edge-smoke (logs: https://ci.redwood.dev/12345) :x: 

Chandra R: another note: TypeScript's `moduleResolution: node` vs `bundler` matters. Some edge runtimes mimic `bundler` resolution. If consumer tsconfig uses `moduleResolution: bundler`, `exports` takes precedence and missing `types` mapping will drop declarations.

Ben K: if adding `types` to exports doesn't fix it, try adding an explicit `export` subpath for types like "./*": { "types": "./dist/*.d.ts" } (but watch packaging). Also verify `package.json` `main`/`module`/`types` alignment.

Sam D: quick test result — adding `types` inside `exports` fixed the TS lookup in the sample (consumer types resolved). runtime ESM/CJS parity still subtle: default import shape differs for the CJS wrapper.

Frank P: for parity we either publish a native ESM build only and provide a small CJS wrapper that re-exports default correctly, or keep CJS main and provide ESM entry. Both okay; the former is cleaner for edge-first.

Chandra R: and update publish playbook doc + add a sample test asserting `import default` shape and `require()` shape. That will catch regressions.

Ben K: agree. Sam, can you open a PR against `samples/entrypoint-interop` with the fix and add a test in `samples/test/entrypoint-resolution.test.ts` that runs Node + a mocked edge bundler resolver? keep the test lightweight.

Sam D: will do. planning to: 1) add `types` into `exports`, 2) add a tiny cjs wrapper that `module.exports = require('./dist/cjs').default || require('./dist/cjs')`, 3) add test and doc note in `devex/publish-playbook.md`. aiming to send PR by EOD.

Ben K: EOD sounds good. thanks for tracking this down. :raised_hands: 

Frank P: also create a short note in release checklist to smoke test edge sample on vercel/edge runtime when releasing dual-pkg builds.

Sam D: added to my PR checklist. will ping here when PR is up.

Ben K: nice one, Sam.
